Three passengers are dead and an investigation is underway after a suspected outbreak of hantavirus ripped through an Atlantic Ocean cruise ship.

While only one hantavirus infection has been confirmed through testing, five others have also fallen ill on the MV Hondius, which was traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde.

The deceased passengers include a senior Dutch couple and a German national, according to Dutch shipowner Oceanwide Expeditions.

Just last month three deaths were reported in Northern California linked to the illness, which came to broad attention with the death of actor Gene Hackman’s wife Betsy Arakawa in February 2025.

Hantavirus is typically spread from through the urine, feces and saliva of infected rodents and is fatal in nearly 4 out of 10 people who are infected.

open image in gallery Cruise ship MV Hondius is seen docking off Cape Verde, Africa, on Sunday as an investigation into suspected cases of hantavirus aboard the vessel continued. Only one case has been traced to a variant of hantavirus so far but three others have died and two crew members have fallen ill with respiratory symptoms ( Reuters )

There are around 150 passengers of 23 nationalities on the ship - including 17 Americans - and no other people with symptoms have been identified. The ship remains anchored off the coast of Cape Verde.

“The exact cause and any possible connection are being investigated. Therefore, the only confirmed case of hantavirus is the passenger who was medically evacuated and is now being treated in Johannesburg,” Oceanwide Expeditions said.

What happened and when

The Oceanwide Expeditions cruise departed from Ushuaia, a resort town in southern Argentina, on March 20. It was due to arrive in Cape Verde on May 4, before heading to Spain’s Canary Islands.

There are 88 passengers and 61 crew members on board.

The first passenger died just weeks into their trip, on April 11.

The passenger, a 70-year-old Dutch man, suddenly developed a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea. His 69-year-old wife helped take his body off the ship upon arriving at the island of St. Helena.

His wife, who was 69, was evacuated to South Africa and later died in a Johannesburg hospital.

It has not yet been confirmed that the couples’ deaths are connected to the current medical situation on board, Oceanwide Expeditions noted.

On the same day, a 69-year-old British man fell seriously ill and was medically evacuated to South Africa. He is in critical but stable condition. He has since been confirmed to have a variant of hantavirus, and is in critical but stable condition.

open image in gallery The MV Hondius, a Dutch cruise ship, can hold 170 passengers and 57 crew members. There are currently nearly 150 people on board ( Reuters )

And over the weekend, a German passenger died. No other information about the passenger or his cause of death has been shared publicly.

Two crew members, who are British and Dutch, also fell ill on the ship.

One has mild respiratory symptoms and the other’s symptoms are severe. It was not said which crew member was more severe.

The ship’s owner said it was working with local and international authorities - including the World Health Organization and the Dutch National Institute for Public Health and the Environment - to begin “possible medical repatriation and next steps.”

“The option of sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife are being considered to be the gateway for disembarkation, where further medical screening and handling could take place,” Oceanwide Expeditions said.

Other passengers are being asked to isolate and practice good hygiene. The ship is also conducting medical evaluations.

“Detailed investigations are ongoing, including further laboratory testing, and epidemiological investigations. Medical care and support are being provided to passengers and crew. Sequencing of the virus is also ongoing,” the World Health Organization explained Sunday.

What to know about hantavirus

open image in gallery Actor Gene Hackman, center right, and his wife Betsy Arakawa, far right, pose with daughters Leslie, center left, and Elizabeth at the premiere of his movie “The Chamber” in October 1996 in Beverly Hills, California. Both Arakawa died after suffering a hantavirus infection in February 2025 ( Getty Images )

Hantavirus is typically tied to exposure to infected rats and mice.

There are dozens of species of the virus circulating worldwide, leading to the acute respiratory disease now known as hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, the condition that killed Arakawa and is most commonly spread by the deer mouse.

Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome initially causes flu-like symptoms that can progress to more a severe illness where people have trouble breathing and need to be intubated.

Symptoms typically start within a week to up to two months after contact with an infected rodent and may include fever, fatigue, muscle aches, dizziness, chills, headaches and abdominal issues, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The disease first emerged during a hantavirus outbreak in the U.S. Southwest in the 1993, with 900 cases reported across the nation since then, federal data shows.

Cases normally occur in rural areas, although animals can enter homes where they may leave urine or feces. Hantavirus can also spread between people - but does so incredibly rarely.

open image in gallery Hantavirus is a virus that spreads through the urine, feces or saliva of rodents, including deer mice. Deer mice commonly spread the kind of hantavirus that can lead to hantavirus pulmonary syndrome ( California Department of Public Health )

But hantavirus pulmonary syndrome is not the only consequence of infection.

Hantaviruses that are largely found in Europe and Asia can cause a hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, resulting in kidney failure, leaky blood vessels and shock. according the CDC says. It may require dialysis.

Symptoms may develop up to two weeks after exposure and include back and abdominal pain, fever, chills, nausea, blurred vision, intense headaches, eye inflammation and redness, flushing of the face and a rash, the CDC says.

There is no specific treatment for hantavirus infection. Patients should receive supportive care, including rest, hydration, and treatment of symptoms.

To reduce the risk of developing an infection, people should seal holes or gaps rodents can get through and place traps around the home.

Hantavirus in the US

Early last month, three people died from hantavirus exposure in a small northern California ski resort town.

The deaths occurred in the town of Mammoth Lakes, which has a population of just over 7,000 and is located in Mono County. Deer mice are widespread in the region.

There was no clear picture of how the third person, a young adult, had contracted the virus, Dr. Tom Boo, the county’s public health officer, said in a statement.

open image in gallery A skier is seen at Mammoth Mountain, located in Mammoth Lakes, California. The northern California resort town has seen three fatal hantavirus cases this year ( Getty )

There was no evidence of mice at the person’s home. While there were some mice at their workplace, it was “not unusual for indoor spaces this time of year in Mammoth Lakes,” he noted.

He said health officials believe deer mouse numbers are high in Mammoth and the Eastern Sierra.

“The occurrence of three cases in a short period has me worried, especially this early in the year,” said Boo. “Historically, we tend to see Hantavirus cases later in the spring and in the summer. We’ve now gone about a month without any additional suspect cases, but remain concerned about the increase in activity.”

Boo’s statement came just a year and two months after a New Mexico medical examiner announced that Arakawa had died from hantavirus pulmonary syndrome.

Both Hackman and Arakawa were found dead in their Santa Fe home. The 95-year-old Academy Award-winning actor is believed to have died of heart disease around a week after his wife, on February 18, 2025.

Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has dismissed suggestions that superstition prompted his side to switch London hotels ahead of their Champions League semi-final second leg against Arsenal, instead claiming their new Shoreditch base was simply "cheaper".

The Spanish club, currently level at 1-1 with the Gunners after last week’s first leg, are preparing for Tuesday’s decisive encounter.

Atleti had previously stayed at the four-star Marriott Hotel in Regents Park before suffering a 4-0 defeat by Mikel Arteta’s side in the league phase back in October.

However, for this crucial last-four clash, they have relocated across the capital to the five-star Courthouse Hotel in Shoreditch, east London.

Reports had suggested Simeone ordered the move, fearing that using the same accommodation as their previous drubbing could bring bad luck.

open image in gallery Atleti are staying at a different London hotel ( PA )

But when questioned about the decision, Simeone responded with a smile: "The hotel was cheaper. That’s why we changed."

Meanwhile, former Manchester City forward Julian Alvarez, who scored a penalty and impressed in the opening leg last week, appears set to overcome an injury to start for Atleti at the Emirates Stadium.

Alvarez, whom Simeone had previously revealed Arsenal are interested in signing, could not complete the first leg and subsequently missed Atleti’s 2-0 victory at Valencia last Saturday. However, the Argentina international, who has netted 20 times for Atleti this season, has travelled to London.

Simeone emphasised Alvarez’s significance, stating: "Julian Alvarez is important in this game because he knows the English league very well. He played really well last week, and I hope he can bring what he needs in the game tomorrow."

The manager also offered broader tactical advice: "As coaches, we have to think about what could happen but it is down to the players. We have to manage our emotions and play as well as possible. The game changes as soon as it kicks off. Over time, you do become patient. It is not about being passive, but calm, and that is what we need in this type of game."

For Antoine Griezmann, who has scored 212 goals in 494 appearances for Atleti, Tuesday’s match against Arsenal could mark his final appearance on Europe’s biggest stage if his team fails to progress.

The 35-year-old Frenchman, who has never won the Champions League, is set to join Major League Soccer side Orlando City at the end of the season.

open image in gallery Julian Alvarez is set to be available for Tuesday's match ( AP )

Despite the personal stakes, Griezmann insisted: "It is not something I am thinking about. I am looking forward to the game tomorrow, it will be a great contest to be part of, and I hope we can have the right attitude and play with the right pressure and build on our second-half performance from the first leg.

“Every time we start a Champions League campaign you can see yourself lifting the trophy, and any child in their bedroom would do the same. We are just two games away now and we have to get it right, tactically defensively and going forward, and of course we need more goals (than Arsenal)."

News.title: Chelsea humiliated by second-string Nottingham Forest to crush Champions League hopes
News.content:
Both sides want and need a win, but for very different reasons.

Chelsea have lost five Premier League matches in a row for the first time since 1993, they are without a manager and to top it all off, haven’t scored during those five sorry defeats, some thing that hasn’t happened since 1912. In short, the club is in trouble and not in the usual Stamford Bridge sense of crisis, they are in actual real disarray.

Today’s hosts lie in ninth, four points off Bournemouth in sixth and in danger of not securing European football next season.

Their opponents come into today’s match in contrasting form. Nottingham Forest are unbeaten in their past six league matches and have scored nine goals in their past two as they try and secure their top-flight safety.

Their 5-0 win against Sunderland secured back-to-back Premier League wins for only the second time this season, and for the first time under Vitor Pereira. Another today at Stamford Bridge would mean a third in a row for the first time last season and go a long way to ensuring they remain in the top flight for another campaign.

The good news for Chelsea is that Cole Palmer could make his first start since a minor hamstring setback left him on the sidelines.

“It has been a difficult period for him,” interim Chelsea manager Calum McFarlane said. “It is the first injury he has pretty much ever had in his career.

“There are obviously games he can impact more, but there have also been plenty of occasions where he has created good chances for others. He can’t control whether those chances are finished - he can only put the ball where it needs to be.

“He’s had some really good games over the past three months. It is just a case of building consistency, so overall I’m really pleased with him.

“He is still a top, top player - one of the best in the world. I’ve got no concerns about him being ready to impact games from now until the end of the season, and hopefully in the World Cup in the big moments for England.”

Stay here for all the team news and action, with kick-off set for 3pm.

News.title: De Zerbi has Spurs believing again as Villa win moves them out of drop zone
News.content:
Spurs were prepared to stump up the £34m fee demanded by Atlético Madrid. Villa proposed a loan with an option to buy which will have frustrated Unai Emery. But not as much as this shocking performance even if, in truth, Spurs have had a poor return from Gallagher up until now.

Having declared last week that “only losers cry”, doubling down on his belief that Spurs will survive then this was the perfect reaction for De Zerbi. It also showed that Spurs have the “big manager” they craved and how they have lucked out in hiring the Italian.

“He makes you feel so good. He brings the best out of you,” Gallagher said. It felt like a universal belief and that might just be enough.

“I am honest. I have one face. If I say all our players are great level it’s because I feel. I don’t want to sell something if I don’t believe in my words,” De Zerbi said. “My job is just to transfer the confidence and believe in themselves. To show passion, to show value, pride.”

He grabbed his shirt just as Palhinha had done. “I love Palhinha,” he added, declaring that this version of Gallagher was like having “12 players”.

Okay, Villa’s Emery made seven changes ahead of Thursday’s momentous Europa League semi-final second leg at home to Nottingham Forest.

But after Spurs scored their second goal there were boos and an exodus of fans to the concourses – and maybe the exits. Just 25 minutes had elapsed. And it could have been four.

That crowd reaction – and there was more – must have provoked a maelstrom of emotions for Emery at a club where he rules the roost and has Messiah-status. On the touchline his demeanour radiated the definition of “if looks could kill”.

For Spurs, De Zerbi may be conferred similar God-like status if he keeps them up. With three games to go, albeit three demanding fixtures, they are a point ahead of West Ham United who have replaced them in the bottom three. It is that tight. But they are up for the fight.

News.title: Snooker on brink of seismic change as Wu surges into 10-7 World Championship final lead
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the World Snooker Championship, as Shaun Murphy takes on Wu Yize.

Yize battled past Mark Allen in his semi-final, with the Englishman missing a match-winning black before Yize claimed a 17-16 victory.

The match-up will be best remembered for a 14th frame that lasted for more than 100 minutes, so we can be sure that at the very least, Yize possesses the necessary stamina for this best-of-35 tie.

For Murphy, Yize is his fourth Chinese opponent in the tournament, having already beaten Fan Zhengyi, Xiao Guodong and Zhao Xintong. His semi-final tie was against John Higgins, as Murphy won 17-15.

Murphy is in decent form this season. He is the 2025 Masters champion, and won the British Open earlier this year. He also was the losing finalist at the Xi’an Grand Prix and the German Masters.

Yize, just 22, also has a 2026 title to his name after lifting the International Championship title, and was beaten in the final of the Championship League earlier in the year.

The youngster is ranked No. 10 in the world, while Murphy is the No. 8 in the standings. At 43, Murphy boasts two decades of experience on his opponent, and rarely appears short of confidence when it comes to his own abilities.

That single-mindedness will be examined under pressure in the Crucible Theatre over the coming two days,

In 2005, Murphy became just the third qualifier to win the World Championship, and he has since lost three finals in the tournament, in 2009, 2015 and 2021. He is the favourite to claim his second win on this Bank Holiday weekend, but Yize’s own undeniable quality makes him a strong contender too.

There are two sessions scheduled for today, and two more for Monday.

News.title: Antonelli claims hat-trick of wins to pile pressure on Russell
News.content:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start today’s Miami Grand Prix pole. Antonelli only finished sixth in the Sprint earlier on Saturday but delivered a time good enough for pole with his first effort in Q3. Antonelli’s lead at the top of the drivers’ standings was cut to seven points to his teammate George Russell after the Sprint but has the chance to extend his lead today.

“It has been an amazing day to be on pole again,” Antonelli said. “It was a difficult start with the Sprint when it did not go our way but super happy with the recovery. I got a bit excited with the last lap in Q3 but the first lap was good enough and I am really happy with that.”

Antonelli will be joined on the front row by Max Verstappen, who was the only driver to properly improve with his second and final run in Q3.

“It is an incredible turnaround for us,” said Verstappen. “I really did not feel in control of the car up until this weekend. I did not know what would happen with it. The team have brought a really good performance upgrade to the car, made it more driveable for me and it really clicked as soon as I jumped in the car here it felt great, or a lot better. For us, to be on the front row, is a bit of a surprise but we take it. It is a massive boost for the whole team and we are heading in the right direction.”

Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc will start third, with McLaren’s Lando Norris joining him on the second row in fourth. Norris won the Sprint earlier on Saturday as part of a McLaren one-two but qualifying was trickier for the team, with Oscar Piastri set to start today’s race in seventh.

“There were little things,” said Norris. “It was a bit windier, the direction was different, temperatures. But same for everyone, right? I think both cars clearly struggled a bit more than yesterday and we need to understand why. At the same time, it’s not like I felt we did a bad job. But other people did a bad job yesterday and today they did the job they should have done.

“Mercedes are just as quick as us. When you look at the GPS from Ferrari and Red Bull, there are many places they are quicker than us. So we just did a very good job yesterday and in the Sprint to win. But qualifying was a little reality check. But it is more where we deserved to be and where we should be honestly.”

The race has been brought forward by three hours due to the threat of thunderstorms. It was set to get under way at 9pm BST (4pm local time) but the FIA and F1 have announced a new start time of 6pm BST.

News.title: ‘My dad’s Henry is 40 years old and still going strong’: Inside the great vacuum cleaner debate
News.content:
The world of vacuum cleaners, it seems, is a tribal one, particularly among Telegraph readers, where brand loyalty is key.

Whether it’s a battle-hardened Henry dragged from job to job, a durable, German-engineered machine or a high-tech Dyson, each choice reflects a different philosophy of cleaning and often says as much about your priorities as it does about your floors.

When we recently updated our guide to the best vacuums, the comments were full of varying opinions and recommendations. So, here’s the advice worth considering next time you’re in the market for a new one.

The people’s champion: Henry

Unpretentious, nostalgic and found everywhere from tradesmen’s vans to family homes, Henry is by far the most highly-rated vacuum cleaner among our readers, and for good reason. Made by British brand Numatic, the vacuum is reliable, indestructible, and even fireproof, as one reader explains.

Henry is “the vacuum cleaner of choice” for David Jones, who regards the brand as the best for helping to manage maintenance on various facilities.

While at home, he prefers to use George: “It is basically a Henry with a wet extraction carpet cleaner bolted on. It can be used as a dry vacuum and works well.”

“I like Numatic stuff in general because its cleaners are powerful, robust and cheap. Parts are readily available, not that I seem to need them much,” he explains.

Jones has tried other vacuums in his work, such as a Dyson stick vacuum, which he found “expensive, flimsy, not very powerful and with limited battery life”.

News.title: Kobbie Mainoo seals Man Utd double over Liverpool to secure Champions League return
News.content:
This may well be one of the most low-key renewals of Manchester United and Liverpool’s rivalry in recent memory, all but assured of Champions League football and out of contention for silverware.

Both teams and managers have something to prove, though. The smart money would appear to be on Michael Carrick and Arne Slot staying in post for the start of next season, but neither would start the campaign with a great deal of security.

The fixture also matters a great deal to both sets of supporters, with Liverpool looking to avenge what was then a shock 2-1 defeat at Anfield. Harry Maguire scored the late winner in what was the high-water mark of Ruben Amorim’s time in charge.

It is a long time since the teams played at Old Trafford, with a 3-0 Liverpool victory last September helping Slot to get his feet under the table. The win would also propel Liverpool to the title.

Carrick has already steered United to wins over Manchester City and Arsenal, and what a trifecta it would be if he could add Liverpool to the list.

Carrick said: “It shows the improvements of the group and getting stronger to be coming into this game in a good position on the back of some good results and trying to achieve moving forward.

“We’re fully aware of the situation in the league and how close it is between us, but that’s not something we’ve focused on.

“It’s a one-off game. They’ve got some good players and they won the league last year, and we respect everything that goes into the game.”

Arne Slot will be without Mohamed Salah owing to a hamstring tweak sustained in the win over Crystal Palace last week and it remains to be seen if goalkeeper Alisson is fit enough to return.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Brilliant Bordeaux underscore heavyweight status by ending Bath’s Champions Cup hopes
News.content:
In the final reckoning, Bordeaux-Bègles underscored their status as the heavyweights of European club rugby by booking their place in a second successive Champions Cup final with the kind of rugby that will remain long in the memory. Without doubt they will be favourites to retain their crown against Leinster in Bilbao.

And yet, while the game got away from Bath in the closing moments in the city where they won their last title 28 years ago against Brive, Johann van Graan’s side took an important step forward in establishing their own credentials as potential future champions.

Parts of this Bath side may be breaking up next season, with Alfie Barbeary joining Saracens and Thomas du Toit returning to his native South Africa to rejoin the Sharks, but the depth of the squad remains intact. Dan du Preez will bolster their back row resources while Billy Sela, who replaced Du Toit off the bench in the final 10 minutes, is a tighthead prop with huge potential.

The champions of England found the step up just beyond them in a contest of high-octane, breathtaking quality and suffocating atmosphere, but they took the defending European champions to the wire. Bath will look back at moments when the pressure of the occasion affected their decision-making and execution, but within a context of the quality of the opposition they were facing.

To beat this Bordeaux team at this stage of the season and when they were backed by over 35,000 supporters was always going to be a massive undertaking, but the experience of taking the fight to them should put Bath in good stead for future European journeys, following their Challenge Cup triumph last year.

It was reminiscent of Saracens’ early forays deep into the European competition, when they lost to Toulon in the semi-final in 2013 and then again to the French side in the 2014 final, before going on to claim the first of three Heineken Cup titles two years later.

There were moments of controversy. Three head-high tackles on Barbeary were not sanctioned and once again the issue of the French director of review footage came under scrutiny, with Van Graan making a rare public complaint afterwards that the match officials did not seem to have the footage available to them to review the incidents.

Sports.title: Why TEN Premier League teams will secretly be rooting for Aston Villa to beat Nottingham Forest in Europa League semis
Sports.content:
AS many as TEN Premier League clubs could still finish sixth and clinch Champions League football if Aston Villa win the Europa League.

Villa go into their Europa semi-final clash against Nottingham Forest 1-0 down on aggregate ahead of the home leg this week.





Both sides rested players going into that crucial game at Villa Park as they bid to reach the final in Istanbul.

Villa made seven changes during their 2-1 home defeat to Tottenham on Sunday in their pursuit of glory.

Forest, meanwhile, made eight changes but still beat Chelsea 3-1 away from home on Bank Holiday Monday.

When the two sides clash on Thursday night, Villa might have quite a supporters cheering them on.

That’s because any team from Bournemouth to Crystal Palace in 15th can mathematically finish sixth and catapult themselves into Europe’s elite if Villa were to clinch glory in the final and finish in the top five.

Brentford, Brighton, Chelsea, Fulham, Everton, Sunderland, Newcastle and Leeds are also in the running in one of the tightest ever races for European football.

Nottingham Forest can only mathematically finish on 51 points despite their incredible recent form.

Andoni Iraola‘s Bournemouth currently occupy sixth spot with 52 points from 35 games.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

This season’s surprise package Brentford are just one point behind them, with Brighton in eighth place on 50 points.

Struggling Chelsea are two points off the Seagulls on 48 and are also level on points with Fulham.

Everton and Sunderland are on 47, Newcastle are on 45, while Leeds and Palace are both on 43.

It’s certainly a low bar given that last season required 66 points to finish in sixth.



Even Nottingham Forest managed an impressive 65 to finish seventh.

Of course, it would be incredibly unlikely that the teams closer to the bottom of the table would get anywhere close to sixth.

The likes of Bournemouth, Brentford and Brighton would have to lose their remaining three games just to give them a chance.

Six English teams qualified for the Champions League last season when Tottenham booked an additional spot by winning the Europa League.

Arsenal, Man City and Manchester United have already qualified for next season’s Champions League, with Liverpool and Villa set to join them.

Sports.title: Real Madrid wonderkid, 19, says his future will be decided by what God tells his WIFE after struggles since £51m move
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN sensation Endrick has claimed his future will be decided by ‘what God tells my wife’ as he continues to shine on-loan at Lyon from Real Madrid.

The 19-year-old scored the clinching goal in Lyon‘s 4-2 win over Rennes at the weekend to move the club into the Champions League places in Ligue 1.





That gives Endrick 15 goal contributions – eight goals and seven assists – in 18 games since joining on loan in January.

He had made just nine starts for Real Madrid in 18 months at the club following his £51 million move in 2024.

But when asked about possibly staying at Lyon after the loan spell, the Brazilian revealed that his wife Gabriely Miranda, 23, will have a decisive say in his future.

He told Globo: “It’s like I always say. If I’m meant to stay here, if I’m meant to return to Real Madrid, if I’m meant to go somewhere else, I’ll do what God tells me. What God tells my wife.



“I thank God for bringing me here, I’m very happy to be here.

“But that’s it, I’ll do what God tells me to do, what God puts in my wife’s head to do.

“Coming to Lyon was one of my best choices, I thank God very much for that because I came to a team that welcomed me.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



“I’m very happy and clearly, God willing, if I go to the World Cup, it will be thanks to the whole of Lyon.”

Endrick’s relationship with Miranda has raised a few eyebrows over the past few years, particularly the revelation they had entered into a ‘relationship contract’, which contained a series of rules and pledges.

Just some of those clauses include being prohibited from developing any kind of addiction, drastic changes in their behavior, and mandating saying ‘I love you’ in all situations.

Endrick is also being banned from having a ‘virtual girlfriend’ on Grand Theft Auto V. Who knew this was a deal breaker?



The increasingly appearent one-sided agreement forbids Endrick from commenting on other girls’ Instagram accounts and reportedly require the pair to base their relationship on ‘respect, understanding and affection’.

But, it seems to be working out. The couple have been married since September 2024, with their marriage coming less than a year after they met.

And last month, the couple announced they are expecting their first child.

Sports.title: Premier League side staggeringly able to qualify for Champions League while still in relegation fight with 3 games left
Sports.content:
THIS Premier League season has treated punters to nail-biting battles at both ends of the table.

But one scrap that has slipped under the radar is amongst the tightly-bunched pack in the middle.





With 35 matches played, there are only 10 points separating sixth-place Bournemouth from Nottingham Forest in 16th.

And that means that Newcastle – with only three games to play – can still technically clinch a Champions League spot or be RELEGATED.

Both outcomes are extremely unlikely but still mathematically possible at this late stage of the campaign.

The Magpies, sitting 13th, are nine points above West Ham in the final relegation place.

The Hammers would make up that nine-point gap by winning their remaining games.

But they would also need a massive goal difference swing totalling 18 goals.

And even in that case, Newcastle would only go down if Leeds, Crystal Palace, Forest and Tottenham also do enough to climb above them.

The other side of the coin might be even more far-fetched.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

At the moment, the top five finishers in the Premier League table will be rewarded with Champions League football next season.

But if Aston Villa finish exactly fifth, and then secure a UCL spot by winning the Europa League, the Prem’s extra qualifying place – earned via English teams’ performances in this term’s European competitions – would apply to sixth place.

And Newcastle are only seven points behind sixth-place Bournemouth with nine points still to play for.

For the stars to align, teams ahead of the Toon would have to slip up monumentally.

But the fact that places in the Championship and Europe‘s top table are both still mathematically possible highlights just how tight things are in the middle of the pack.



Newcastle snapped a five-game losing streak by beating Brighton on Saturday and finish the season with games against Forest, West Ham and Fulham.

Sports.title: Chelsea fans stream out of Stamford Bridge before full-time as Nottingham Forest supporters taunt them with cheeky chant
Sports.content:
EMBARRASSED Chelsea fans flooded out of Stamford Bridge in the 75th minute after being battered by Nottingham Forest.

The visitors chanted, “Is there a fire drill?” at the home supporters, who booed their team off at half-time once more.





And they have good reason to be frustrated.

Forest relentlessly mocked them from the first whistle, ridiculing Blues fans with chants of “Are you Tottenham in disguise?” and “You’re just a bus stop in Fulham.”

Well, actually, they might be Tottenham in disguise.

Since Thomas Frank was sacked by Spurs on February 11th, Chelsea have the lowest points tally of ANY team in the Premier League and would sit at the bottom of the table since that date.



Joao Pedro‘s disallowed goal in the 75th minute brought on a chorus of “We nearly scored” from the home fans, and groans filled the ground when nine minutes of injury time were announced.

Forest fans, obviously, retorted, “We want more,” and “Can we play you every week?”

In fact, when Joao Pedro scored a stunning bicycle kick in those nine minutes, half of the seats in Stamford Bridge were empty.

Before that late consolation, they hadn’t scored a Premier League goal since their 4-1 win over Aston Villa on the 4th March, and they hadn’t scored a league goal at home since their 1-1 draw with Burnley on the 21st February.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

An almost-empty Stamford Bridge roared boos once more when the full-time whistle eventually went.

And it looks as though they will need a miracle to be playing in the Champions League next season.

But while the result will have left Chelsea fans feeling sick, seeing what happened to promising youngster Jesse Derry will have struck a similar chord.

The 18-year-old was making his full debut for the Blues at Stamford Bridge on Bank Holiday Monday.



But his dream quickly turned into a nightmare after a worrying clash of heads with Zach Abbott, leading to a lengthy delay.

There was huge concern for Derry, with his father Shaun – the former QPR captain, reportedly visibly upset after watching the scenes.

The youngster received oxygen on the pitch before being stretchered off and he has now been taken to hospital in an ambulence for further treatment.

Chelsea confirmed the news after their 3-1 defeat to Forest as they revealed Derry was conscious and talking after the initial worry.

Sports.title: Chelsea give Jesse Derry injury update after debutant was rushed to hospital following sickening clash of heads
Sports.content:
DERRY UPDATE Chelsea give Jesse Derry injury update after debutant was rushed to hospital following sickening clash of heads

CHELSEA have given an update on the condition of young star Jesse Derry after he was rushed to hospital.

Derry was handed his Premier League debut for the Blues going into their clash with relegation-threatened Nottingham Forest.





But after an impressive start to the contest, his afternoon was cut short after a sickening clash of heads with Forest defender Zach Abbott.

Derry contested a header in the box with Abbott, who arrived late and clattered into the Chelsea youth prospect, before both men fell to the ground in pain.

The 18-year-old was treated on the pitch and eventually stretchered off on oxygen, before being rushed to the hospital.

And now the club have released a statement giving fans an update on his condition.

Chelsea wrote: “Jesse Derry has been taken to hospital as a precaution following his first-half substitution during today’s Premier League game against Nottingham Forest.

“Jesse is conscious, talking and undergoing precautionary checks.

“We wish him a speedy recovery and thank the medical staff for their swift response.“

Manager Calum McFarlane added his own update on the star following the match, as well as on Robert Sanchez, who also had to be withdrawn from the game following a head injury,



McFartane said: “We’re hearing positive signs from Jesse and Rob [Sanchez] and I hope the Nottingham Forest players are okay as well.

“But I’m pleased for Jesse’s performance. I thought he performed well while he was on the pitch, but there’s probably more important things to think about right now.”

Derry is the son of former Crystal Palace midfielder Shaun Derry and joined Chelsea from the South London side last summer.



The winger has made 29 appearances for the Under-21s this season, scoring 12 goals and providing four assists.

His only senior minutes this season have come during FA Cup clashes against Championship sides Wrexham and Hull City.

Following his injury, the youngster was replaced by Liam Delap, while Abbott was swapped for defender Neco Williams.

It was just one blow in what was a nightmare day at the office for Chelsea as they fell to a 3-1 loss.

Taiwo Awoniyi opened the scoring for the visitors in the opening minutes of the game, before Igor Jesus doubled their advantage after Malo Gusto‘s silly concession of a penalty.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Blues received a penalty of their own for the clash that injured Derry, but Cole Palmer could only drill his effort into the hand of Forest keeper Matz Sels.

Sports.title: Chelsea ratings: Jesse Derry’s promising debut ruined by shocking injury as three Blues defenders score 1/10
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are under a cloud, and Nottingham Forest are on cloud nine after joining a long list of teams to beat the Blues at Stamford Bridge without reply.

It took less than two minutes for the Blues to fall behind at home when former Strasbourg winger Dilane Bakwa beat Marc Cucurella and crossed into Taiwo Awoniyi, who was unmarked at the back post.





A matter of minutes later, Forest had a second after a stupid pull of the shirt by Malo Gusto on Awoniyi, with the resulting penalty sent straight down the middle by Igor Jesus.

Chelsea had chances, as Enzo Fernandez rattled the post and full debutant Jesse Derry fired over, with the 18-year-old winning a penalty just before half-time, which unfortunately saw him stretchered off.

Cole Palmer, though, missed it, and his side were booed off at half-time once more.

Forest got their third, and Awoniyi’s second, early in the second half when Morgan Gibbs-White put in a low cross for the striker to tap into an empty net.

Joao Pedro found the back of the net with a close-range finish late in the game, only for it to be overturned by VAR, typically.

This is how SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the Blues…

Robert Sanchez – 4

It’s difficult to give him the blame for either of the goals, and his distribution wasn’t bad.

The penalty being rolled down the middle perhaps made him look silly, but if he had stood there and it was in the corner, we would be saying the same thing.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He was brave to come and punch the ball against the onrushing Morgan Gibbs-White, but left the pitch with blood pouring down his face and his head bandaged up after the incident.

Malo Gusto – 1

His decision to pull Awoniyi’s shirt in the 11th minute was utterly stupid, and had Chelsea two goals down before 15 minutes had even gone.

Played much higher in the second half as the Blues attempted to get back into the game, but couldn’t create anything on the right wing.

Tosin Adarabioyo – 1

His distribution from the back line was really poor, and if there was a game that showed where Chelsea could’ve used Levi Colwill, it was this one.



His lazy lump from the back led to the opening goal, and he was poorly positioned far too often.

A shambolic performance before being hooked at half-time and replaced by Colwill.

Trevoh Chalobah – 1

Between him and Tosin, neither of them could get a grip on Awoniyi for the opener, if he was two inches taller, maybe he would’ve been fine.

The second Awoniyi goal looks even worse for him, as the ball flew straight past him into the feet of the Nigerian forward.



Marc Cucurella – 2

Was beaten far too easily by Bakwa for the opening goal, and generally struggled against the former BlueCo-owned winger.

He was nowhere to be seen as Gibbs-White burst down the right and crossed for Forest’s third.

Cucurella almost redeemed himself with a cross into Joao Pedro, who eventually found the back of the net, before it was ruled out for offside.

Moises Caicedo – 5

Was good on the ball in terms of his passing, but Chelsea needed him to be more creative in midfield in this game.



He made the most defensive actions of any player, as you may expect, with several interceptions and recoveries.

Caicedo was the best of a bad bunch in midfield for the Blues.

Romeo Lavia – 4

Looked to make things happen for the Blues in the middle of the park when he got on the ball and attempted to play forward on the half-turn.

Unfortunately for him, it just wasn’t really happening, as was the case for many in blue.

Cole Palmer – 2

Until now, Palmer at least had penalties to cover up what has been a pretty shambolic season.



There has been plenty of debate as to whether Cole Palmer should play as a number 10 or a right winger for the Blues and for England in the summer.

Well, today he played out wide, and we’re still unsure; he just does not look like the same player anymore.

Taking on his man seems like a thing of the past, with his touch too heavy and his shots either high or wide.



Missing a penalty just before half-time personified the level of confidence he seems to have been playing with this season.

Enzo Fernandez – 4

Fernandez was very, very quiet in the first half after a captain’s performance against Leeds in the FA Cup semi-final.

He came closest to scoring for the Blues when he stroked the ball onto the post in the first half with his right foot, but that was about all there was to say about him.

In the second half, Elliot Anderson came on for Forest and showed him what a £100m midfielder should look like, undoubtedly winning the battle between the two number eights.

Jesse Derry – 7

Undoubtedly Chelsea’s best player on the day, which says a lot about his talent, but also the state of the Blues right now.



He looked to always take on his man and played with the youthful desire of a player who can go to the very top – showcased no better than him winning the penalty that brought his side back into the game.

He was let down by his teammates after putting in a dynamic attacking showing with plenty of clever dribbles – before his afternoon was harshly cut short by a sickening clash of heads.

Joao Pedro – 7

He showed flashes of the player that Stamford Bridge fell in love with earlier this season, but wasn’t given good enough service to really make things happen up top.

He did well to finish at the second time of asking from close range in the second half, only for the goal to be ruled out for offside by VAR.

Later produced a remarkable bit of improvisation to claw a goal back for the Blues late on, but it was too late to give his side any hope of a comeback.



SUBS

Liam Delap (for Derry 45′) – 3

Failed to make any real impact after coming on and replacing Derry, who looked far more creative than the £30million striker.

Levi Colwill (for Adarabioyo 46′) – 5

Great to see him back on the pitch, and he stepped in well with his tackles when required.

Chelsea looked better with him playing, but they could’ve hardly looked worse…

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Andrey Santos (for Lavia 58′) – 3

Didn’t make any notable impact in midfield and wasn’t as good as Lavia, whom he replaced.



Filip Jorgensen (for Sanchez 67′) – 5

Not much was asked of him after replacing the injured Sanchez.

Sports.title: Chelsea 1 Nottingham Forest 3: Blues lose sixth straight league game but clash marred by sickening head injuries
Sports.content:
ASTON Villa beware.

Nottingham Forest B won this at a canter so heaven help Unai Emery’s side in the second leg of the Europa League semi final on Thursday night.





Or so you would think.

But Chelsea were so bad, yet again, it was hard to tell whether Forest boss Vitor Pereira gambled with his team selection.

Or simply knew his second string would be good enough to defeat a club still mired in crisis despite reaching the FA Cup final..

All the talk before the match was whether Pereira was at risk of making Forest the first team to compete in the Champions League and the Championship in the same season. Or worse.

Not against this shower of a Chelsea team and squad

The distressing sight of teenage winger Jesse Derry being taken off on a stretcher following a clash of heads, and Cole Palmer failing to convert the resulting penalty, were shocks.

But otherwise this was self-inflicted business as usual for the Blues in an absolutely dismal season of Stamford Bridge performances.

By the time goalkeeper Robert Sanchez also had to go off midway through the second half after his own coming together with Morgan Gibbs-White, the home side were three goals down to Taiwo Awoniyi’s brace and an Igor Jesus penalty.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And their supporters were singing the familiar songs against majority owners Clearlake Capital and head honcho Behdad Eghbali.

They have every right to be furious.

Chelsea last lost six league games in a row back in November 1993.

Only Joao Pedro’s spectacular stoppage-time goal prevented them from doing so without scoring for the first time in their history.



Failure to win made it mathematically impossible to finish in the top five and earn Champions League qualification.

While Forest are two games from making their own way there, the Blues could well miss out on European football altogether.

Yet it seemed like a day when Chelsea would end their pointless, goalless, hapless five-game Premier League run.

In addition to the apparent gift of the Forest teamsheet, there was good news in the returns of captain Reece James, after seven weeks out with a hamstring problem, and of long-term casualty Levi Colwill.



The comeback of the central defender, who had ruptured an ACL in the first pre-season training session, felt like a particularly good omen.

It was Colwill who had scored the only goal at the City Ground on the final day of the last campaign to seal Chelsea’s return to the Champions League.

Instead, Chelsea’s hopes of a first league clean sheet since January 17 died inside 100 seconds.

Dilane Bakwa, signed by Forest from the Blues’ sister club Strasbourg last summer, beat Marc Cucurella far too easily down the right and crossed. Awoniyi was left unchallenged to head the ball home



Chelsea did respond, with Enzo Fernandez sending in a dangerous cross and then hitting the post.

But the home side were soon two down. Bakwa crossed, Malo Gusto pulled back Awoniyi, and although referee Anthony Taylor did not see it, VAR did.

Gusto avoided a red card because the Forest striker would not have reached the ball so it was not denial of a goalscoring opportunity..



Awoniyi made sure the Blues paid a real penalty by firing home from the spot.

The home fans and players were shellshocked and frustrated. Chelsea did not threaten and when Tosin Adarabioyo hit a long ball straight out for a Forest goalkick, boos rang around Stamford Bridge.

Forest went close-ish twice more and the away supporters were enjoying every minute.

Joao Pedro dived in vain in search of a penalty but in the last minute of the half, Taylor gave the Blues a lifeline.

The referee pointed to the spot after Zach Abbott challenged Derry in the air and the pair clashed heads.



Palmer had 10 minutes to think about his spotkick while poor Derry was prepared for the stretcher.

With England boss Thomas Tuchel watching from the stands, the Chelsea No 10 hit it low and pretty hard. But Matz Sels saved it brilliantly with a strong right hand before blocking the follow-up.

Some Chelsea fans recovered enough from the shock to boo again when the half-time whistle finally went.



They cheered when Colwill’s half-time introduction was announced. Meanwhile Pereira put on A-listers Gibbs-White, Elliot Anderson and Nikola Milenkovic.

And within seven minutes Gibbs-White teed up Awoniyi to complete his hat-trick.

The striker seemed to be ahead of the ball when his team-mate crossed but technology said not.

Sanchez and Morgan Gibbs-White collided and both had to leave the field with bandaged heads.

Pedro thought he had pulled one back but had been offside before his initial shot.



During nine minutes of stoppage time, the Brazilian finally found the net with a fabulous overhead kick.

But nothing would have been consolation for this performance.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some of the home sections had long been less than half-full and those fans who remained booed half-heartedly.

Supporters of Forest B sang, “The Reds are staying up”.

Sports.title: Southampton will make World Cup star their first summer signing if they are promoted to the Premier League
Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON will sign on-loan striker Cyle Larin if they are promoted.

The Canadian, 31, has nine goals in 20 appearances for Saints since joining on loan this January, bagging six in his last eight Championship games.





SunSport can reveal that Larin’s loan deal from Spanish side Mallorca included an obligation to buy for £3.4million upon promotion.

Larin has played a huge role in pushing Tonda Eckert’s side into the Championship play-offs, where they face Middlesbrough and he is in line to start the first-leg at the Riverside.

Southampton, who were 14th when Larin arrived but finished fourth, have an option to buy even if they are not promoted back to the Premier League.

No talks have been held over a potential permanent contract with the striker at this stage, but Saints would be keen to keep him if they are still in the Championship next season.



Larin spent the first half of the season out on loan at Feyenoord, scoring just one goal in 15 appearances in all competitions.

And the Canada international looks set for action in this summer’s World Cup, which will be co-hosted by his home country.

As SunSport reported, Southampton are also keen to keep goalkeeper Daniel Peretz on a permanent basis.

The Israel international has had also been key in driving Saints into the top six after joining on loan from Bayern Munich in the January window.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

There is no obligation to buy for the goalkeeper, but a £7m option. Peretz would be open to staying but has hinted his future will depend on whether Saints are in the Premier League or not.

He told SunSport last month: “For sure it [promotion] will have an impact. But it’s too early because I’m not thinking.

“We are playing so often that really I still didn’t even think about the next season.

“I just know that I’m super happy here and I get a lot of love and I’m feeling I’m performing well and I have really good connection with my teammates, with the club, with the staff, with the fans.

“It’s not something I take for granted and you don’t have it quite often. So I have it here. I’m really happy here but let’s finish the season in the best way and then we will be smarter to take decisions.”

Sports.title: Antoine Griezmann desperate to take final Atletico Madrid chance ahead of Arsenal showdown
Sports.content:
Antoine Griezmann desperate to take final Atletico Madrid chance ahead of Arsenal showdown

Antoine Griezmann will leave his beloved Atletico Madrid at the end of the season, but wants to go out on a high by beating Arsenal on the way to winning the Champions League

View 2 Images Atletico Madrid forward Antoine Griezmann speaks ahead of Arsenal clash

Antoine Griezmann has admitted he still becomes the “little boy” dreaming of Champions League glory before every season.

‌



Atletico Madrid veteran Griezmann, 35, will leave the club at the end of the season to move to Major League Soccer but is still desperate to lift the trophy before he goes.

‌



France superstar Griezmann has never won the Champions League, played but missed a penalty in the 2016 final and has one last shot at the glory he dreamed of all those years ago.

‌



He said: “Every time we start a Champions League campaign, you can see yourself lifting the trophy. Every little boy, every child in their bedroom does the same.

“The Champions League is always different. What has helped me is that I've always wanted to play in it since I was a child. I'm not much for talking to young players, but rather for setting an example.

Diego Simeone reveals real reason for late Atletico Madrid change before Arsenal clash READ MORE :

Four Arsenal players miss training before crunch Atletico Madrid clash in Champions League READ MORE :

“Approaching the match with enthusiasm, joy... And during the match, I offer tactical or technical guidance where I can help. When to slow down or speed up. That's where I help most. Koke is more about talking and motivating.

‌



“Every time we start the Champions League, you obviously see yourself lifting the trophy, and every team or player dreams of it.

“We're two games away, and tomorrow we need to be tactically and defensively sound and continue the same level we showed in the second half at home.”

Griezmann insists he has no regrets about deciding to leave - but is determined to grasp one last chance. He added: “I’m looking forward to the match. It’s a great experience to play in and enjoy. We hope the level of play will be the same as in the second half.

‌



View 2 Images Griezmann will leave Atletico Madrid at the end of the season

“I was always clear, my idea was to stay here because incredible things could be done. Here we are, with the chance of another final. And the team knows it.

“I’m focused on tomorrow’s game, on what my teammates will need. I’m not thinking about the games I have left. I’m just focused on being fresh and having good legs.

‌



“That final in 2016 was very different. I was under a lot of stress. Everything was happening at a very fast pace, and I didn't know when to slow down.

“Now I'm more well-rounded and calmer. I approach matches with more composure and joy. These are moments you think will come back, and then they don't. Playing in a semi final isn't for everyone.”

Sports.title: Diego Simeone reveals real reason for late Atletico Madrid change before Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone reveals real reason for late Atletico Madrid change before Arsenal clash

Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone will lead his side as they take on Arsenal on Tuesday night, with a place in the Champions League final at stake

View 2 Images Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone speaks ahead of the Champions League semi vs Arsenal

Diego Simeone has revealed Atletico Madrid have switched hotels - and joked it was to save money.

‌



Atletico Madrid stayed in a Marriott near Regents Park when Arsenal thrashed them in the league phase back in October.

‌



In Spain it has been reported that Atletico boss Simeone switched hotels this time to a different venue in nearby trendy Shoreditch because he is superstitious.

‌



But when asked whether he is superstitious and also whether Atletico are in a better place now than last year, the normally very serious Atletico boss came back with a quip.

Simeone said: “We are doing better than in October, and the hotel was cheaper! That’s why we changed.”

Viktor Gyokeres issues perfect response after starting to prove Arsenal doubters wrong READ MORE :

Four Arsenal players miss training before crunch Atletico Madrid clash in Champions League READ MORE :

Atletico go into the second leg on level terms with Arsenal but there was a hint of what they are capable of in the second half. That is why the Spanish giants cannot be written off as they chase a place in the final but Simeone says he is relaxed and ready for the return leg.

‌



Simeone said: “Well as coaches we have to think about what could happen but it is down to the players. We have to manage our emotions and play as well as possible.

“The game changes as soon as it kicks off. Over time, you do become patient. It is not about being passive, but calm, and that is what we need in this type of game. Of course I want them to repeat the second-half performance from the first leg, and if it is as simple as that then it would be great.

View 2 Images Atletico Madrid are all level after a controversial 1-1 draw in Madrid last week

‌



“I know you are always looking for headlines and interesting quotes, but the reality is that we want the match to start now, and get involved, and if we play well we have a better chance of winning. We will try to play to our strengths and so will Arsenal.

“We have played the game we needed to do to get here with the right level of intensity and we hope our leaders and as a team we can do what we need to do.

“We are confident in terms of what we want with the game, but it is not just down to us. We are convinced about what we need to do. Whatever plan is chosen, we will stick with until the end.

Article continues below

“I just need to work hard and we are clear about what we need to do, and we hope to transmit that as clearly as possible because we want to put in a great performance.”

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly has exactly what Man Utd are looking for after ‘tough’ Arsenal treatment
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly has exactly what Man Utd are looking for after ‘tough’ Arsenal treatment

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been linked with a move to Manchester United, with Mikel Arteta's tactical shift showing the teenager's versatility

View Image Myles Lewis-Skelly of Arsenal (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly has sent a clear signal to Manchester United that he can operate in midfield as well as at left-back. The Gunners defender was deployed in the centre of the park during Saturday's commanding 3-0 victory over Fulham.

‌



United have been strongly linked with strengthening their midfield ranks this summer as they gear up for their return to Champions League football.

‌



Sunday's triumph over Liverpool secured a top-five finish for United, and attention will swiftly turn to the summer transfer window, where the Red Devils will be able to enter the market for new additions.

‌



Midfield remains an area United are widely expected to address, with Casemiro anticipated to leave the club when the season draws to a close.

Rio Ferdinand fires brutal personal dig at Jamie Carragher as feud escalates after Man Utd win READ MORE :

Viktor Gyokeres issues perfect response after starting to prove Arsenal doubters wrong READ MORE :

Separately, reports over recent months have linked United with a potential move for Lewis-Skelly, with the England international having struggled for regular game time at Arsenal this campaign compared to his breakthrough season last term.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta handed Lewis-Skelly a midfield start at the weekend, making it abundantly clear that the 19-year-old is more than capable of performing in multiple positions.

‌



Reports have indicated that Arsenal may be forced to sell one of their first-team players this summer in order to fund their own transfer activity, though it remains uncertain whether Lewis-Skelly could be among those to leave.

Arteta discussed his decision to deploy Lewis-Skelly in midfield, with the Arsenal boss acknowledging he has been "tough" on the youngster amid speculation linking him with a potential move to United.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"Maybe I should have done it [start Lewis-Skelly in midfield] earlier, I don’t know," Arteta stated over the weekend. "I have to do things when I believe that the player is ready, the team is ready and the opponent is the right one.

"It was a big risk. If it works, it's great. If we lost the game I know what would have happened. 'How do you play a kid at this age, in this scenario, in a position that he has not played all season?'

"I knew that, but I had the feeling it was the right game for him.

Article continues below

"He fully deserves it. I have been tough on him. He had a spectacular season last year when he jumped into the first team, then had some difficult moments after that. But he stayed very humble, very focused and I knew he was ready."

Sports.title: Man Utd learn possible Champions League opponents next season after £16m boost
Sports.content:
Man Utd learn possible Champions League opponents next season after £16m boost

Manchester United appear to already know two of their opponents for the Champions League next season after sealing qualification with a win over Liverpool

View 2 Images Manchester United already know some of their potential Champions League opponents for next season (Image: (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images))

Manchester United's win over Liverpool has sealed their return to the Champions League, with Michael Carrick accomplishing his goal of guiding the club back to European football's premier competition.

‌



While precise figures won't be confirmed until next season, the 13-time Premier League champions are set to pocket approximately £16.1m for reaching the league phase of the Champions League - based on this year's figures. United's prize money will only increase from that point, though none of it is guaranteed.

‌



They stand to earn £1.8m for each victory in the league phase and £600,000 for every draw. While there is considerable work to be done over the summer to ensure United are equipped to compete on several fronts - including the appointment of a permanent manager - supporters can already begin to fantasise about trips across the continent.

‌



After a season without European football, there will be a real hunger for the biggest fixtures to be back on their schedule. The new league phase, which United have yet to experience, consists of eight matches.

Clubs are divided into four pots determined by their UEFA coefficient over the preceding five years. Each side faces two opponents from every pot, playing four matches at home and four away.

Bruno Fernandes embarrasses Ruben Amorim with eye-opening Man Utd admission READ MORE :

Casemiro transfer bombshell as Matheus Cunha hints at Man Utd U-turn over exit READ MORE :

With 36 teams in the competition, nine sides are placed in each pot. As things stand, Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Paris Saint-Germain, Inter Milan, Manchester City, Arsenal, Barcelona and Bayer Leverkusen are expected to makeup Pot 1.

‌



Atletico Madrid could yet nudge one side out of the pot should they eliminate Arsenal and go on to lift the Champions League trophy. Leverkusen have yet to guarantee their place in next season's competition, which would see Atletico slot in as the 10th-highest ranked side at present.

United cannot be drawn against clubs from their own nation, meaning they are set to face two of Bayern, Real Madrid, PSG, Inter, Barcelona and either Atletico or Leverkusen. It gets considerably more complicated from there, but alongside Atletico or Leverkusen, Borussia Dortmund are also destined for Pot 2. Porto will join them having wrapped up the Portuguese title ahead of Benfica.

Jose Mourinho's side and Sporting are ranked highly enough to warrant a place in Pot 2, but are locked in a battle for second in Portugal and will also need to come through a playoff round. With Tottenham, Frankfurt and Atalanta all ranked above Manchester United - who sit 21st in the coefficient - yet failing to qualify, and only one of Sporting or Benfica able to enter the tournament, United have a reasonable chance of landing in Pot 2, though it remains on a knife-edge.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 2 Images Kobbie Mainoo scored the goal that sealed Champions League qualification for Manchester United (Image: Matt West/Shutterstock)

Villarreal and PSV Eindhoven have also secured their spots in next season's Champions League. The Spanish outfit are expected to be placed in Pot 4, with the Dutch champions landing in Pot 3.

‌



Despite guiding the team back into the continent's elite competition, Carrick doesn't want his squad to 'over celebrate' even though he's satisfied with the outcome. "I think the work that's been done and the players, the way they've performed, and the teams that we've played against and got good results against, I think it's something that we can take a lot from, for sure," Carrick said. "I think it was well in the distance, a little bit, if we're honest, at one point.

"So there has been a lot of good work to put us in a position with three games to go and get that sealed. But it's not something we've spoke about as a group really

"I think it's not something we over-celebrate. I think it's a step. We want more. We want to be finishing higher up the league but, certainly there is huge credit deserved that goes to the players and the staff, for putting us in this position, at this stage."

Sports.title: 'I coached Bruno Fernandes at Man Utd – he's a nightmare in training and we clashed after game'
Sports.content:
'I coached Bruno Fernandes at Man Utd – he's a nightmare in training and we clashed after game'

Bruno Fernandes clashed with his former Manchester United coach after failing to do one thing

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes has been described as a "nightmare" in training (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Steve McClaren has revealed that he clashed with Bruno Fernandes when he was on the coaching staff at Manchester United. A fuming Fernandes failed to acknowledge the club's fans after crashing out of the Carabao Cup to Newcastle in 2023.

‌



McClaren - who served as Erik ten Hag's assistant from 2022 to 2024 - was angry with the Portugal international's behaviour and called him out for it. Speaking to The Athletic, the former England boss revealed: "We only clashed once. He didn’t clap the fans, so we had a bit of a row about that.

‌



"I think it was Newcastle’s win 3-0 at Old Trafford (Carabao Cup fourth round, November 2023). I was more upset with the team and the players. It was bad, but the next day we kissed and made up. He is excellent with fans 99 per cent of the time."

‌



McClaren praised Fernandes' fervent passion and said the way he wears his heart on the sleeve reminds him of Roy Keane. He added: "We had one spell when we said to Roy, ‘You’ve got to calm down a bit’.

Alan Shearer shakes head as four Liverpool stars singled out after Man Utd loss READ MORE :

Bryan Robson tells Man Utd to hire Michael Carrick TODAY in strong message to board READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Because it was beginning to be a problem. Through the trouble he got into, he used to miss five or six games a season. He tried to calm down, and he was rubbish. "So we said, ‘Forget that, be yourself, it’s all right, we’ll miss you for five games, don’t want you to be a pussycat on the field’.

‌



"And Bruno is the same." McClaren explained why that very quality left him having a "nightmare" in training, as he continued: "When I used to have to be the referee in training, he’s a nightmare. It’s just passion. He’s fit, he runs around, he scores, he assists, his numbers are phenomenal."

View 3 Images Steve McClaren revealed he clashed with Bruno Fernandes (Image: Getty Images)

Fernandes has been a fan favourite since his £47million move to Old Trafford in 2020. With 107 goals and 106 assists for the club, the Portugal international, 31, has been a shining light in a dismal period for United since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013.

‌



In McClaren's 25-year managerial career, the Englishman places Fernandes as one of the top five best players he's ever coached. "I remember his first game at Old Trafford, he picked out long balls and diagonals," he recounted. "I thought, ‘Missing link’. He wants to do everything. He’s really one of the top five players I’ve coached.

"He’s got scrolls of vision, that je ne sais quoi. I’ve seen things in training, you go, ‘Wow’. His attitude, his professionalism is first class. He’s first in, last away. Last on the pitch, doing shooting, practising all day to be better."

View 3 Images The Red Devils clinched Champions League football after beating Liverpool (Image: Phil Duncan/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Article continues below

Fernandes' leadership and consistent performances have led United to the Champions League next season. Their place in the competition was confirmed after their 3-2 win over Liverpool on Sunday.

The 31-year-old's future at Old Trafford has remained unclear but Mirror Football understands that securing Champions League football will be enough to keep Fernandes in Manchester.

Sports.title: Chelsea issue Jesse Derry update after star taken to hospital with head injury
Sports.content:
Chelsea issue Jesse Derry update after star taken to hospital with head injury

Chelsea winger Jesse Derry had to be stretchered off and taken to hospital as a result of a nasty clash of heads in Monday's home game against Nottingham Forest

View 2 Images Jesse Derry was taken to hospital after being stretchered off (Image: Alex Pantling)

Chelsea have said that Jesse Derry is "conscious" and "talking" after the teenager was hospitalised following a sickening clash of heads in Monday's game with Nottingham Forest.

‌



The 18-year-old was making his first ever Premier League in the Blues' 3-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge. But he suffered a serious looking injury on the stroke of half-time when he collided with Nottingham Forest defender, Zach Abbott.

‌



Derry was taken away on a stretcher after receiving lengthy treatment with Sky Sports later confirming he had been taken to hospital. Chelsea have since issued a further positive update on the youngster.

‌



"Jesse Derry has been taken to hospital as a precaution following his first-half substitution during today’s #PL game against Nottingham Forest," the club said via their X account.

Nottingham Forest and Spurs flip Premier League relegation battle with West Ham in danger READ MORE :

Chelsea youngster taken off on stretcher after sickening clash of heads READ MORE :

"Jesse is conscious, talking and undergoing precautionary checks. We wish him a speedy recovery and thank the medical staff for their swift response."

With Derry and Abbott both being withdrawn before the break following their clash of heads, two other players were involved in a nasty collision later in the game.

‌



Morgan Gibbs-White was introduced at half-time but was bandaged up before being taken off following a clash with Robert Sanchez, who was replaced himself by Filip Jorgensen. Thankfully, both players were able to walk off the pitch despite being left with cuts to the head.

View 2 Images Derry was making his first Premier League start (Image: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC)

Nottingham Forest won the match 3-1 to all but clinch Premier League safety despite Vitor Pereira making EIGHT changes to the team that beat Aston Villa in the first leg of their Europa League semi-final in midweek.

Article continues below

Taiwo Awoniyi broke the deadlock in the first two minutes before Igor Thiago doubled Forest's lead from the penalty spot. Awoniyi grabbed his second and Nottingham Forest's third goal early in the second half with Joao Pedro bagging a late consolation for Chelsea.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest and Spurs flip Premier League relegation battle with West Ham in danger
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest and Spurs flip Premier League relegation battle with West Ham in danger

Games are running out for teams at the foot of the Premier League to save themselves with Tottenham and West Ham trading places following a huge victory for Roberto De Zerbi's men

View 3 Images Taiwo Awoniyi and Igor Jesus were on target in a big win for Nottingham Forest (Image: Sebastian Frej/MB Media)

Nottingham Forest were the big winners of the weekend in the Premier League relegation battle as they all but clinched safety with a stunning 3-1 triumph at Chelsea.

‌



And with Tottenham also recording a seismic away win over Aston Villa, it's West Ham who are now staring relegation in the face after dropping back into the bottom three just as the sand in the hourglass begins to run dry.

‌



Forest have managed to put daylight between themselves and the two beleaguered London clubs in recent weeks as a result of an upturn in form which has been timed almost to perfection. Few, though, would have been expecting an afternoon to remember in the capital when Vitor Pereira made eight changes to the side that beat Aston Villa in the first leg of their Europa League semi-final in midweek.

‌



But they were leading inside 90 seconds at Stamford Bridge courtesy of Taiwo Awoniyi. And they were two goals to the good on 15 minutes when Igor Jesus diligently dispatched a penalty kick after Malo Gusto mindlessly dragged back the Brazilian's strike partner inside the area.

Chelsea youngster taken off on stretcher after sickening clash of heads READ MORE :

Unai Emery gets verdict on Premier League integrity as defeat by Tottenham questioned READ MORE :

Cole Palmer spurned a golden opportunity to get Chelsea back into it before half-time when he failed to convert another spot-kick, given after a sickening clash of heads involving the unfortunate Jesse Derry in the Forest area.

And Awoniyi took full advantage by adding a third for Forest early in the second half to nudge them six points ahead of West Ham with three games left to play.

‌



View 3 Images Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham side took a huge stride towards safety (Image: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

The weekend started badly for the Hammers, who were poor in defeat against Brentford. And things got even worse on Sunday night when Tottenham picked the perfect time to win consecutive Premier League games for the first time since August 2025, beating a much-changed Aston Villa team 2-1.

While Forest now look out of reach for West Ham, albeit not quite so mathematically, Nuno Espirito Santo's side are still in touching distance with Tottenham.

‌



View 3 Images West Ham are now in the bottom three with just three games remaining (Image: Clive Rose)

But with a trio of challenging games remaining, Spurs could retain their Premier League status without picking up another point unless West Ham can muster up something special between now and their home finale against Leeds.

As it is, Forest can almost taste safety. It also now feels like Spurs sense a route to it after weeks of darkness. For West Ham, it's now a case of hoping they can engineer one last twist to spare them from doom.

‌



GAMES REMAINING

Nottingham Forest: Newcastle (H), Man Utd (A), Bournemouth (H)

Tottenham: Leeds (H), Chelsea (A), Everton (H)

West Ham: Arsenal (H), Newcastle (A), Leeds (H)
